# Vflo

::: {#o1 .subject cue=lead name="Vflo"}

*Image: Vflo splashpage.jpg.*

**V*flo*** is a commercially available, [physics](wikipedia://en/22939)-based distributed [hydrologic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrologic) model generated by [Vieux & Associates, Inc.](http://www.vieuxinc.com) V*flo* uses [radar rainfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather_radar) data for [hydrologic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrologic) input to simulate distributed [runoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runoff_model_%28reservoir%29).[^o2][^o3] V*flo* employs [GIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GIS) maps for parameterization via a desktop interface.[^o4] The model is suited for [distributed](wikipedia://en/3523316) hydrologic forecasting in post-analysis and in continuous operations. V*flo* output is in the form of [hydrographs](wikipedia://en/881602) at selected [drainage network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_system_%28geomorphology%29) grids, as well as [distributed](wikipedia://en/3523316) runoff maps covering the watershed. Model applications include civil [infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrastructure) operations and maintenance, [stormwater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stormwater) prediction and [emergency management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_management), continuous and short-term surface water [runoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runoff_model_%28reservoir%29), recharge estimation, [soil moisture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil_moisture) monitoring, [land use](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_use) planning, [water quality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_quality) monitoring, and water resources management.

:::

## History {#History}

V*flo* considers the spatial character of the [parameters](wikipedia://en/25065) and precipitation controlling hydrologic processes, and thus improves upon lumped representations previously used in [hydrologic modeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrological_modelling). Historical practice has been to use lumped representations because of computational limitations or because sufficient data was not available to populate a [distributed](wikipedia://en/3523316) model database.[^o6] Advances in [computational](wikipedia://en/5926) speed; development of high-resolution precipitation data from [radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather_radar) and satellites; and availability of worldwide digital data sets and [GIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GIS) technology makes distributed, physics-based modeling possible.[^o7] V*flo* is designed to take advantage of the spatial variability of high resolution [radar rainfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather_radar) input, [GIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GIS) datasets, and hydraulic channel characteristics. Because it is [physics](wikipedia://en/22939)-based, it produces [hydrographs](wikipedia://en/881602) based on conservation equations and the hydraulics of the [drainage network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_system_%28geomorphology%29), and can be employed in locations where there are no [rain gauges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain_gauge) or previous modeling studies. In addition, V*flo*’s network approach makes models scalable from upland [watersheds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_basin) to river basins using the same [drainage network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_system_%28geomorphology%29).

::: {#o9 .definition cue=heading name="Formulation"}

## Formulation {#Formulation}

V*flo* is suited for distributed hydrologic forecasting in post-analysis and continuous operations. V*flo* models may be [calibrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calibration) by loading precipitation maps for historical events and comparing simulated volume/peak [hydrographs](wikipedia://en/881602) to observed hydrographs. Elevation data are taken from a [digital elevation model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_elevation_model). A vector channel representation is employed. Parameterization utilizes digital data sets at any resolution, including [LIDAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LIDAR) terrain data and other digital maps of [impervious area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permeability_%28earth_sciences%29), soils, and land use/cover. V*flo* is developed to utilize multi-sensor inputs from [radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather_radar), satellites, [rain gauges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain_gauge), or model forecasts. The kinematic wave analogy is used to represent hydraulic conditions in a [watershed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_basin).

:::

## Specific simulation options {#Specific_simulation_options}

- Rainfall input
  - [Radar-rainfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather_radar): UF, [ASCII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESRI_grid), [NEXRAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NEXRAD) Level II, [CSV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comma-separated_values)
  - Satellite data
  - [Rain gauges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain_gauge), [Barnes objective analysis](wikipedia://en/22703042)
  - Quantitative precipitation estimates from model forecasts
  - Multi-sensor precipitation estimates
- [Evapotranspiration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evapotranspiration)
- [Snowmelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowmelt)
- [Sensitivity analysis](wikipedia://en/620083)
- Inundation mapping
- [Infiltration](wikipedia://en/3159833)
  - Enhanced [Green-Ampt](wikipedia://en/3159833#Green-Ampt) infiltration module with initial saturation calibration factor (slider), saturated hydraulic conductivity, wetting front suction, effective porosity, and soil depth
  - Abstraction and impervious area parameters with [ASCII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESRI_grid) import/export
- Overland flow
  - Manning's equation
- Channel flow
  - Kinematic Wave Analogy
  - Modified Puls
  - Observed flow
  - Looped rating curve modification (Jones method)
  - Rating curves and cross sections for complex hydraulics
- Flood watch points
- Design storms, SCS, user generated

::: {#o12 .application cue=heading name="Applications"}

## Applications {#Applications}

- Continuous and short-term surface water [runoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surface_runoff)
- Stormwater prediction and management
- [Flash flood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flash_flood) forecasting
- Operational flood alert
- Flood event reconstruction
- Design Storm development
- Recharge estimation
- Soil moisture monitoring
- [Hydrology](wikipedia://en/13435) and [Hydraulics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydraulics) studies
- [Land use](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_use) planning scenarios
- [Water quality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_quality) studies
- [Hydropower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydropower) management
- [Hydrology](wikipedia://en/13435) education
- [Hydrologic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrologic) research

:::
